title: Tree traversals
objective: Visit every node of a tree in pre-order, in-order and post-order with one recursive walk.

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): binary search trees: inorder, preorder and postorder tree walks

simplifies: Level-order (row by row) needs a queue instead of recursion; it is the same idea as BFS, covered in the graphs lessons.

quiz.prompt: In-order on a binary search tree gives the keys…

options.explanation: Right. Left side (smaller), then the node, then the right side (bigger), at every level.

options.text: In the order they were inserted
options.explanation: Insertion order shapes the tree, but in-order always reads it back sorted.

quiz.prompt: Which order visits a node only after both its children?

options.explanation: Right. Useful when children must be handled first, like deleting a tree or adding up sizes.
Pre-order visits the node before its children.
In-order visits it between its left and right sides.
